- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is falling, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., first 5–7 days); adjust by smoothing toward recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 10-day moving average for smoothing.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often fails to capture sustained downward trends; apply downward bias of 2–4% if sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model may misinterpret sentiment as bullish; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment-price divergence.
